_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for India covering Indus Valley civilisation, Vedic period, Maurya Empire (Ashoka), Gupta golden age, Chola/Pallava/Rashtrakuta southern kingdoms, Delhi Sultanate, Vijayanagara Empire, Mughal Empire, Maratha Confederacy, European trading companies, British Raj, independence movement (Gandhi, Nehru), Partition 1947, republic, Green Revolution, liberalisation 1991, nuclear power, IT revolution, and Modi era.

ethnic_groups.name: Indo-Aryan
ethnic_groups.notes: North India; includes Hindi belt, Bengali, Marathi, Gujarati, Rajasthani, Punjabi, Bihari, Odia, Assamese speakers; dominant in Gangetic plain

ethnic_groups.name: Dravidian
ethnic_groups.notes: South India; Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam speakers; distinct language family; Indus Valley connections debated; anti-Hindi movement heritage

ethnic_groups.name: Scheduled Tribes (Adivasi)
ethnic_groups.notes: Indigenous/tribal; 705 recognised tribes; Gond (largest, ~13M), Bhil, Santal, Munda, Oraon, Khasi, Mizo, Naga, Kuki, Bodo, Toda, Jarawa, Sentinelese; forest-dwellers; constitutionally protected

ethnic_groups.name: Scheduled Castes (Dalit)
ethnic_groups.notes: Formerly 'untouchable'; cross-cutting with Indo-Aryan/Dravidian; Ambedkar led constitutional protections; reservations (affirmative action); continuing discrimination

ethnic_groups.name: Sino-Tibetan/Tibeto-Burman
ethnic_groups.notes: Northeast India (Seven Sisters + Sikkim); Naga, Mizo, Manipuri, Bodo, Khasi (Austroasiatic actually), Lepcha, Monpa; culturally distinct; many Christian; cross-border with Myanmar/China

ethnic_groups.name: Other
ethnic_groups.notes: Anglo-Indian; Parsi (Zoroastrian, ~60,000); Jewish (Bene Israel, Cochin, Baghdadi); Siddi (African descent, Gujarat/Karnataka)

independence.notes: Republic Day January 26, 1950 (constitution); Partition created India and Pakistan

country_profile.notes_unique: World's most populous country (2023+); largest democracy; 22 scheduled languages; nuclear-armed; space programme (Chandrayaan, Mangalyaan); 28 states and 8 UTs; caste system still socially significant

geography.terrain: Himalayas north; Indo-Gangetic plain; Deccan Plateau south; Western/Eastern Ghats; Thar Desert west
geography.notes: 7th largest country; world's most populous (1.43B); Himalayas world's highest mountain range; monsoon climate critical for agriculture; Andaman & Nicobar Islands; Lakshadweep.

economy_extended.notes: World's 5th largest economy; fastest growing major economy; IT/BPO global leader (Bengaluru, Hyderabad); UPI digital payments revolution; Make in India manufacturing push; demographic dividend; informal sector ~80% employment.

health.notes: World's largest vaccination programme; Ayushman Bharat (500M beneficiaries, world's largest health insurance); 'pharmacy of the world' (generic drugs); COVID made 2B+ vaccine doses; AIIMS premier hospitals; air pollution major health burden.

food_agriculture.notes: World's #1 producer of milk, pulses, spices, tea, jute; #2 rice and wheat producer; Green Revolution transformed food security; MSP procurement system; world's largest food subsidy programme (800M people); water stress critical.

energy.notes: World's 3rd largest energy consumer; coal 70% of electricity; massive solar expansion (target 500 GW renewable by 2030); Jamnagar world's largest refinery; energy poverty despite 100% electrification claim; LNG imports growing.

transport.notes: Indian Railways: world's 4th largest network, 13M passengers/day; highway expansion (Bharatmala Pariyojana); Delhi Metro largest in India; bullet train (Mumbai-Ahmedabad) under construction; IndiGo world's fastest growing airline.

tourism.notes: 42 UNESCO World Heritage Sites; incredible diversity of attractions; medical tourism growing ($9B); spiritual/yoga tourism; Incredible India campaign; domestic tourism massive (2B+ trips/year).

legal_system.notes: World's largest democracy; independent judiciary (activist Supreme Court); PIL (Public Interest Litigation) unique; sedition law repealed 2023; CAA and farm laws controversies; personal law system (Hindu/Muslim/Christian).

human_rights_gender.lgbtq_legal_status: Legal (Section 377 struck down 2018; no marriage recognition)
human_rights_gender.notes: World's largest democracy but declining press freedom; Section 377 decriminalized 2018; gender-based violence concern (Nirbhaya case); caste discrimination; religious polarization; Women's Reservation Bill passed 2023.

security_stability.notes: Nuclear weapons state; Kashmir conflict and Line of Control; Naxalite-Maoist insurgency; India-China LAC tensions (Ladakh); northeast insurgencies declining; world's 4th largest military budget; border disputes with Pakistan and China.

cultural_heritage.notes: One of world's oldest civilisations (Indus Valley, 3300 BCE); birthplace of Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism, Sikhism; Sanskrit literature; zero and decimal system; Bollywood largest film industry by output.

comparative_rankings.notes: 5th largest economy but low per-capita rankings; demographic dividend; space programme (Chandrayaan-3 Moon landing 2023); IT and pharmaceutical powerhouse; environmental challenges acute.
comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global. 'rank' = 1 is best/largest.

current_leader.name: Narendra Modi
current_leader.title: Prime Minister
current_leader.notes: BJP; Hindu nationalist; Gujarat CM 2001-2014; 'Make in India'; demonetisation 2016; 370 abrogation (Kashmir); Ram Mandir; third term 2024 (NDA coalition)

president.name: Droupadi Murmu
president.title: President (ceremonial)
president.notes: First tribal (Santal) president; first president born in independent India

former_leaders.name: Jawaharlal Nehru
former_leaders.notes: First PM; INC; architect of modern India; Non-Aligned Movement; Nehruvian socialism; died in office

former_leaders.name: Indira Gandhi
former_leaders.notes: INC; Nehru's daughter; Bangladesh liberation 1971; Emergency 1975-1977; Operation Blue Star; assassinated by Sikh bodyguards October 1984

former_leaders.name: Rajiv Gandhi
former_leaders.notes: INC; youngest PM; IT modernisation; Bhopal gas tragedy; assassinated by LTTE 1991

former_leaders.name: Atal Bihari Vajpayee
former_leaders.notes: BJP; Pokhran-II nuclear tests 1998; Kargil War 1999; Golden Quadrilateral highway; moderate Hindu nationalist

former_leaders.name: Manmohan Singh
former_leaders.notes: INC/UPA; economist; architect of 1991 liberalisation (as FM); nuclear deal with US; RTI Act; died 2024

910.name: Indus Valley Civilization
910.description: The Harappan civilization — one of the world's earliest and largest urban cultures — with sophisticated city planning, undeciphered script, maritime trade with Mesopotamia, and the mysterious decline.

sub_clusters.name: Early and Mature Harappan Phase
sub_clusters.description: The emergence and zenith of the Indus Valley Civilization at Mohenjo-daro, Harappa, Dholavira, and Rakhigarhi, featuring advanced urban planning, standardized weights, the Great Bath, and extensive maritime trade.
key_events: Mohenjo-daro and Harappa flourish as among the world's largest cities with populations over 40,000 (c. 2500 BC)
Indus merchants trade with Mesopotamia, evidence found in Akkadian texts as 'Meluhha'

sub_clusters.name: Late Harappan Decline
sub_clusters.description: The gradual decline of Harappan urbanism, possible causes including climate change and river shifts, the deurbanization and dispersal of populations, and the Cemetery H culture transition.

910.name: Vedic Period and Mahajanapadas
910.description: The Indo-Aryan migrations, the composition of the Vedas, the emergence of Hinduism, the rise of the Sixteen Mahajanapadas, the births of Buddhism and Jainism, and the first Indian empires.

sub_clusters.name: Early and Later Vedic Period
sub_clusters.description: The composition of the Rigveda, the Indo-Aryan settlement of the Gangetic plain, the development of the varna system, the philosophical Upanishads, and the transition from pastoral to agricultural societies.
key_events: Composition of the Rigveda, one of the oldest religious texts in the world (c. 1500–1200 BC)

sub_clusters.name: Mahajanapadas and New Religions
sub_clusters.description: The Sixteen Mahajanapadas including Magadha and Kosala, the lives of Gautama Buddha and Mahavira, the Nanda dynasty, Alexander's invasion of the Punjab, and Chanakya's plotting.
key_events: Gautama Buddha attains enlightenment and begins teaching the Dharma (c. 528 BC)
Alexander the Great invades the Punjab and defeats King Porus at the Hydaspes (326 BC)

910.name: Maurya Empire
910.description: India's first great empire under Chandragupta Maurya, Ashoka's transformation from warrior-king to Buddhist pacifist, the world's first welfare state, and the spread of Buddhism across Asia.

sub_clusters.name: Chandragupta and Imperial Foundation
sub_clusters.description: Chandragupta Maurya's overthrow of the Nanda dynasty with Chanakya's guidance, the defeat of Seleucid Greeks, Kautilya's Arthashastra, and the creation of the Indian subcontinent's first unified empire.
key_events: Chandragupta Maurya founds the Maurya Empire with Chanakya's guidance (c. 321 BC)

sub_clusters.name: Ashoka the Great
sub_clusters.description: Emperor Ashoka's bloody conquest of Kalinga, his remorseful conversion to Buddhism, the Rock and Pillar Edicts promoting dharma, the Third Buddhist Council, and missions spreading Buddhism to Sri Lanka and Central Asia.
key_events: Ashoka's conquest of Kalinga (c. 261 BC) — horrified by the carnage, he embraces Buddhism
Ashoka erects pillars and rock edicts across the subcontinent, the earliest decipherable Indian inscriptions

920.name: Post-Mauryan and Classical Period
920.description: The Shunga and Satavahana dynasties, the Indo-Greek and Kushan kingdoms, and the golden age of the Gupta Empire — India's classical zenith of art, science, mathematics, and literature.

sub_clusters.name: Shunga, Satavahana, and Kushan Kingdoms
sub_clusters.description: The post-Mauryan fragmentation, the Shunga dynasty's Hindu revival, the Satavahana kingdom of the Deccan, the Kushan Empire's Silk Road connections, and the flourishing of Gandharan and Mathura art.

sub_clusters.name: Gupta Golden Age
sub_clusters.description: The Gupta Empire's classical zenith: Aryabhata's mathematics and astronomy, Kalidasa's literature, the Ajanta cave paintings, the decimal numeral system, and the flowering of Hindu temple architecture.
key_events: Aryabhata calculates pi, proposes the earth's rotation, and develops the place-value system (499 AD)
Kalidasa writes Shakuntala and Meghaduta, masterpieces of Sanskrit literature (c. 400 AD)

920.name: Regional Kingdoms and Temple Age
920.description: The post-Gupta regional kingdoms — Harsha, Chalukyas, Pallavas, Rashtrakutas, Cholas — the age of great temple construction, the bhakti movement, and the Chola maritime empire.

sub_clusters.name: Harsha and Early Medieval North
sub_clusters.description: Emperor Harsha's brief reunification of northern India, Xuanzang's visit documenting Indian civilization, the Rajput kingdoms, and the fragmentation into competing dynasties.

sub_clusters.name: Deccan and South Indian Dynasties
sub_clusters.description: The Chalukya-Pallava rivalry, the Rashtrakuta Empire's Kailasa temple at Ellora, the Pallava shore temples of Mamallapuram, and the development of Dravidian temple architecture.

sub_clusters.name: Chola Maritime Empire
sub_clusters.description: The Chola dynasty's extraordinary naval empire dominating the Indian Ocean, Rajendra Chola's invasion of Southeast Asia, the Brihadeeswarar Temple, and the spread of Indian culture across maritime Asia.
key_events: Rajendra Chola I launches a naval expedition to Southeast Asia, conquering Srivijaya (1025 AD)
Brihadeeswarar Temple completed at Thanjavur — one of India's greatest architectural achievements (1010 AD)

930.name: Delhi Sultanate
930.description: The five dynasties of the Delhi Sultanate, the transformation of northern India under Muslim rule, the repulsion of the Mongols, and the cultural synthesis of Indo-Islamic civilization.

sub_clusters.name: Slave and Khalji Dynasties
sub_clusters.description: Qutb ud-Din Aibak's founding of the Sultanate, Iltutmish and Razia Sultana, the Khalji dynasty's repulsion of Mongol invasions, and Alauddin Khalji's conquests extending to the Deccan.
key_events: Razia Sultana rules as the only female sovereign of the Delhi Sultanate (1236–1240)
Alauddin Khalji repels multiple Mongol invasions and conquers the Deccan (1296–1316)

sub_clusters.name: Tughlaq and Late Sultanate
sub_clusters.description: Muhammad bin Tughlaq's eccentric policies, Timur's devastating sack of Delhi, the Sayyid and Lodi dynasties' decline, and the fragmentation into regional sultanates — Bengal, Gujarat, Bahmani, and Vijayanagara.
key_events: Timur sacks Delhi, massacring 100,000 prisoners (1398)

930.name: Mughal Empire
930.description: The Mughal Empire — one of the world's great civilizations — from Babur's conquest through Akbar's tolerant synthesis, Shah Jahan's architectural masterpieces, and Aurangzeb's controversial expansion.

sub_clusters.name: Babur, Humayun, and Akbar
sub_clusters.description: Babur's victory at Panipat, Humayun's exile and restoration, and Akbar the Great's creation of a multicultural empire with the Din-i Ilahi, mansabdari system, and architectural wonders at Fatehpur Sikri.
key_events: Babur defeats Ibrahim Lodi at the First Battle of Panipat, founding the Mughal Empire (1526)
Akbar abolishes the jizya tax and creates a policy of sulh-i-kul (universal peace) (1564)

sub_clusters.name: Shah Jahan and Aurangzeb
sub_clusters.description: Shah Jahan's golden age of architecture including the Taj Mahal, the Red Fort, and the Peacock Throne, the war of succession, and Aurangzeb's vast but unsustainable expansion and religious conservatism.
key_events: Shah Jahan completes the Taj Mahal, one of the world's greatest architectural masterpieces (1653)
Aurangzeb's reimposition of the jizya and Deccan wars overstrain the empire (1679–1707)

930.name: Maratha and Sikh Empires
930.description: The rise of Shivaji's Maratha Empire challenging Mughal hegemony, the Maratha Confederacy's domination of India, and the Sikh Empire under Maharaja Ranjit Singh in the Punjab.

sub_clusters.name: Shivaji and Maratha Confederacy
sub_clusters.description: Shivaji Bhonsle's founding of the Maratha kingdom through guerrilla warfare against the Mughals, the Peshwa-led Maratha Confederacy dominating 18th-century India, and the eventual defeat by the British.
key_events: Shivaji crowned as Chhatrapati, founding the Maratha Empire (1674)
Third Battle of Panipat — Ahmad Shah Durrani defeats the Maratha Confederacy (1761)

sub_clusters.name: Sikh Empire
sub_clusters.description: Maharaja Ranjit Singh's powerful Sikh Empire in the Punjab, the modernized Khalsa Army, the Koh-i-Noor diamond, and the Anglo-Sikh Wars ending in British annexation.
key_events: Maharaja Ranjit Singh captures Lahore and founds the Sikh Empire (1799)

940.name: British Raj
940.description: British colonial rule from the Battle of Plassey through the Crown Raj, the Indian Rebellion of 1857, the rise of nationalism, Gandhi's non-violent movement, and the traumatic Partition.

sub_clusters.name: Company Rule and 1857 Rebellion
sub_clusters.description: The East India Company's conquest through diplomacy and war, the exploitation of Indian resources and deindustrialization, and the great Indian Rebellion of 1857 ending Company rule.
key_events: Indian Rebellion of 1857 — sepoys, princes, and peasants revolt against Company rule; Crown takes over governance

sub_clusters.name: Crown Rule and Nationalist Movement
sub_clusters.description: Queen Victoria's proclamation, the Indian National Congress, the partition of Bengal, the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, and the rise of Mahatma Gandhi as the leader of Indian nationalism.
key_events: Jallianwala Bagh massacre — General Dyer orders troops to fire on unarmed civilians at Amritsar (1919)

sub_clusters.name: Gandhi, Independence, and Partition
sub_clusters.description: Gandhi's Salt March, the Quit India Movement, Subhas Chandra Bose's INA, the communal violence, and the Partition of India creating Pakistan — accompanied by one of history's greatest mass migrations.
key_events: Gandhi's Salt March galvanizes the Indian independence movement (1930)
Partition of India — independence accompanied by massive communal violence and 15 million displaced (August 1947)

950.name: Nehru Era and Non-Alignment
950.description: Jawaharlal Nehru's founding vision for independent India — democracy, secularism, socialism, non-alignment — the integration of princely states, the constitution, and the humiliating China war.

sub_clusters.name: Independence and Constitution
sub_clusters.description: The integration of 562 princely states by Sardar Patel, the assassination of Gandhi, B.R. Ambedkar's drafting of the world's longest constitution, and the first general elections.
key_events: Mahatma Gandhi assassinated by Nathuram Godse (30 January 1948)
India adopts its Constitution — the world's longest written constitution (26 January 1950)

sub_clusters.name: Nehruvian Nation-Building
sub_clusters.description: Nehru's Five-Year Plans, the Non-Aligned Movement, the IITs and 'temples of modern India,' the linguistic reorganization of states, and the shock defeat in the 1962 Sino-Indian War.
key_events: India co-founds the Non-Aligned Movement at the Bandung Conference (1955)
China defeats India in the 1962 border war, shattering Nehru's 'Hindi-Chini bhai-bhai' vision

950.name: Indira Gandhi and Emergency Era
950.description: Indira Gandhi's dominant leadership, the 1971 Bangladesh war, India's nuclear test, the Emergency's authoritarian interlude, Operation Blue Star, and her assassination.

sub_clusters.name: Indira's Ascendancy and Bangladesh War
sub_clusters.description: Indira Gandhi's 'Garibi Hatao' populism, bank nationalization, the decisive victory in the 1971 war creating Bangladesh, and India's first nuclear test ('Smiling Buddha').
key_events: India defeats Pakistan and liberates Bangladesh in a 13-day war (December 1971)
India conducts its first nuclear test — 'Smiling Buddha' — at Pokhran (1974)

sub_clusters.name: Emergency and Assassination
sub_clusters.description: The 21-month Emergency suspending civil liberties, Indira's electoral defeat and return to power, Operation Blue Star at the Golden Temple, and her assassination by Sikh bodyguards.
key_events: Indira Gandhi declares a State of Emergency — democracy suspended for 21 months (1975–1977)
Indira Gandhi assassinated; anti-Sikh riots kill thousands in Delhi (October–November 1984)

960.name: Economic Liberalization and Rise
960.description: The 1991 economic reforms transforming India into a market economy, the IT revolution, nuclear tests, the Gujarat riots, the Mumbai attacks, and India's emergence as a global power.

sub_clusters.name: 1991 Reforms and IT Revolution
sub_clusters.description: Manmohan Singh's liberalization ending the License Raj, the IT and outsourcing boom, the 1998 nuclear tests, the Kargil War, the Gujarat riots, and India's rapid economic growth.
key_events: Finance Minister Manmohan Singh launches economic liberalization, dismantling the License Raj (1991)
India conducts Pokhran-II nuclear tests; Pakistan responds with its own tests (1998)

sub_clusters.name: UPA Era and Growth
sub_clusters.description: The Congress-led UPA governments, NREGA rural employment, the nuclear deal with the US, the 2008 Mumbai attacks, the Right to Information Act, and anti-corruption movements.
key_events: Mumbai terrorist attacks by Lashkar-e-Taiba kill 166 people (November 2008)

960.name: Modi Era and Geopolitical Rise
960.description: Narendra Modi's BJP government, Hindu nationalism, demonetization, Article 370 abrogation, CAA-NRC debates, the COVID-19 crisis, and India's rise as the world's most populous nation and fifth-largest economy.

sub_clusters.name: Modi First Term
sub_clusters.description: Narendra Modi's sweeping electoral victory, Make in India, demonetization of high-value currency notes, the GST rollout, surgical strikes, and rising Hindu nationalist politics.
key_events: Demonetization — 86% of India's currency withdrawn overnight (8 November 2016)

sub_clusters.name: Modi Second Term and Global Ascent
sub_clusters.description: Abrogation of Article 370 in Kashmir, the Citizenship Amendment Act protests, the COVID-19 crisis and vaccine diplomacy, India's G20 presidency, Chandrayaan-3 moon landing, and becoming the world's most populous nation.
key_events: India revokes Article 370, ending Jammu & Kashmir's special status (August 2019)
Chandrayaan-3 makes India the fourth nation to land on the Moon (August 2023)

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
